brief_rationale: All five responsibility-chain requirements were met with no in-chain errors. The doctor performed comprehensive newborn triage, reconciled the medical record timeline with caregiver-reported context, clarified medications including the initially missed iron supplement, provided specific follow-up owners and timing, and obtained clear teach-back. One high-order point (HO2) was completed through active verification that distinguished old severe diagnoses from current normalized findings, preventing both panic and false reassurance. No second high-order point was meaningfully completed, capping the grade at Strong per the rubric.

citations.quote: 血小板210×10⁹/L 已回到正常新生儿范围，不算低；血红蛋白108 g/L 对目前日龄的宝宝属于“轻度早产/生理贫血”阶段，不需要额外打针或住院，继续口服葡萄糖酸亚铁 2.2 ml 一天两次即可

closure_assessment.explanation: The episode closed safely after the caregiver completed the follow-up visit, received confirmation that current lab values were reassuring, and had clear instructions for ongoing observation, medication, and scheduled neurodevelopmental follow-up. All blocking residual risks were addressed through the in-person follow-up completion and teach-back.

high_order_assessment.explanation: Doctor actively prevented both opposite errors: confirmed that delayed mobile snippets of severe diagnoses represented resolved hospital course (not current deterioration), and verified that normalized PCT/platelets support current stability while still requiring scheduled neurodevelopmental follow-up for the HIE history.

The discharge medications and follow-up instructions were already documented; the doctor provided clarification but did not perform a significant chain repair beyond the minimum required medication reconciliation duty.

While the doctor closed the episode safely and acknowledged the need for neurodevelopmental follow-up, the explicit framing that acknowledges residual longitudinal risk while closing the current episode was not distinctly demonstrated beyond the minimum duty to refer for follow-up.
